recommended_approach: Use a Mantaflow gas simulation (Domain + Flow), bake it, and render the Domain with a volume material driven by the simulation grids—specifically using the Principled Volume shader’s built-in blackbody emission driven by the simulation’s temperature field (typically the “temperature” volume attribute/grid). For a small orange fire plume, keep the shading centered on Blackbody emission (Principled Volume: Blackbody Intensity + Temperature/Temperature Attribute) and use the simulation’s density/flame fields only to shape the plume and control opacity.

required_objects: At least one Domain and one Flow (Domain must exist before baking).
mantaflow_workflow.rendering_step: Assign a volume material to the Domain to use simulation outputs (density/temperature) for shading.
mantaflow_workflow.bake_note: Save the .blend before baking; bake the cache to generate final sim data.

principled_volume_shader_inputs_from_doc.Color Attribute: color (typical for smoke simulations, if present/needed)
principled_volume_shader_inputs_from_doc.Blackbody Intensity: Set to 1 for physically accurate intensity (docs note)
principled_volume_shader_inputs_from_doc.Temperature_(Kelvin): Principled Volume ‘Temperature’ input is in kelvin; higher values emit more.

volume_info_node_outputs_from_docs.Density: Scalar density of smoke inside the Fluid Domain
volume_info_node_outputs_from_docs.Flame: Scalar density of fire inside the Fluid Domain (all three outputs are the same per docs)
volume_info_node_outputs_from_docs.Temperature: 0–1 maps to 0–1000 kelvin (per docs); useful to drive Blackbody/Principled Volume fire shading (may require scaling to kelvin when used directly).

shading_guidance_from_docs.fire_blackbody: Fire can be rendered with blackbody emission using Principled Volume.
shading_guidance_from_docs.custom_volume_setup_option: For more control, manually combine Volume Absorption/Scatter/Emission and use volume attributes (e.g., density/temperature) via Attribute node(s).

Domain must exist before baking (workflow order matters).
Save the blend-file before baking (recommended in the workflow excerpt).

Be careful about temperature units when wiring shader nodes: Principled Volume expects kelvin for its Temperature input, while the Volume Info node’s Temperature output is documented as 0–1 mapping to 0–1000 K.
alternative_approaches: Use a custom volume shader network (Volume Absorption + Volume Scatter + Volume Emission) instead of Principled Volume, and drive those nodes with simulation attributes (density/temperature) via Attribute node(s).

Use the Volume Info node’s Flame/Temperature outputs to drive emission directly (instead of relying on Principled Volume’s Temperature Attribute) when you want node-level artistic control over fire intensity and color.
